title: Accelerate the complete current P104 forward scalar replay by 3.87x
body:
The complete forward scalar checker for the current PR6453 word now has an explicit sparse integer engine. Five alternating fresh-process triples reduce median complete command time from **1.0791 to 0.2789 seconds, a 3.87x speedup**. Function-only time falls from0.9793 to0.1747seconds. All15 runs return the same complete scalar receipt. This is a local scalar-verification measurement, not a full supplier or multiplier speedup, and it changes no kappa.

The initial shared-denominator port was extended with exact coefficient caching and a cheaper equivalent growth guard. A separate packed-radix engine was implemented and checked; its complete command median is0.4181seconds, so sparse rows remain the recommended interface. The techniques are credited prior work; the new result is their complete current forward consumer, conformance evidence and measured comparison.

[Proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/3a95dded3393c07a520c48fb1fecb259fa25504c/research/p104-forward-integer-replay/PROOF.md), [receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/3a95dded3393c07a520c48fb1fecb259fa25504c/research/p104-forward-integer-replay/RESULT.json), [measurements](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/3a95dded3393c07a520c48fb1fecb259fa25504c/research/p104-forward-integer-replay/BENCHMARK.json).

Normal and optimized CPython3.12.13 checks pass on all35,749 event prefixes of the current and clean predecessor words, covering28,563,451 changed-row coefficient positions including zeros. The retained Fraction update is the comparator; unchanged rows are covered by induction. All19 retained scalar guards, helper control flow, all seven original scalar controls,13 additional rejection cases,3,840 arithmetic cases and a complete COPY variant pass. Source corruption, cache eviction, lost ADD, omitted guard and changed benchmark controls reject. The current word has770public inputs,29owned fields,45lifetimes,peak13,paid rank mass5925 and scalar allowance131560, unchanged.

The sparse engine preserves original rejection messages on this corpus. The experimental packed bound pass rejects one invalid public dimension earlier; no identical error-order contract is claimed for that experiment. Both representations have exact arithmetic proofs. There is no verdict cache, probabilistic fingerprint, source replacement or monkey patch.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-forward-integer-replay
python3.12 -I -B research/p104-forward-integer-replay/run.py sparse
```

The21-file committed package passes byte/mode and official export checks. Read-only Git-free, empty-PATH normal/optimized export replays agree and leave all22 exported files unchanged. Hosted plan and package replay [pass](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41557010827) at this exact head. Full-history preflight is unrun in this shallow checkout; all five predecessor files are retained and authenticated, so replay needs no side-branch object, network or Git. Independent human and proof-kernel acceptance are unclaimed.

Only `research/p104-forward-integer-replay/` is added. Native phases, independent transpose, physical caller, pricing, compiler/outer admission and all five selected assumptions remain separate. The next task is explicit full-caller integration with complete receipt/control comparison and whole-process measurement. No wider speedup is inferred.

[Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5600#discussioncomment-19363428). Canonical main7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a, revision8/selected6030, remained unchanged at the submission refresh. Live work through6500 was checked: PR6479 is native replay, PR6021 is the earlier transpose checkpoint, the active interval-root claim is pricing, and PR6499 selected-word integer records is a rounded physical interface. None is counted here. Sparse/historical/unpublished coverage limits remain.

Prepared for Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents. [NOTICE](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/3a95dded3393c07a520c48fb1fecb259fa25504c/research/p104-forward-integer-replay/NOTICE) credits Ali Romman, David Arias, Cinna Davis, Gareth Davidson, DreamingOfClouds, Erwan L, Rohan Arun, ywz65, woklerx, Nick Petalas and Sagar Thakrar, plus all retained P104/native/compiler lineage. Shared denominators and Kronecker substitution are classical. No merge, closure or frontier change is requested.

Verified head: `3a95dded3393c07a520c48fb1fecb259fa25504c`.
